linear-pottery-culture.name: Linear Pottery culture
linear-pottery-culture.summary: A major European Neolithic archaeological culture (about 5500–4500 BC), marking early agriculture's spread along the Danube, Elbe and Rhine, named for its simple incised pottery.

danubian-culture.name: Danubian culture
danubian-culture.summary: Term coined by archaeologist Vere Gordon Childe for the first farming societies of Central and Eastern Europe, beginning around 5500 BC along the Danube valley, including the Linear Pottery culture.

paris-basin.name: Paris Basin
paris-basin.summary: A major geological region of France formed as a large sedimentary sag since the Triassic period, bordered by several ancient upland massifs.

funnelbeaker-culture.name: Funnelbeaker culture
funnelbeaker-culture.summary: A Neolithic archaeological culture in north-central Europe, about 4100 to 2800 BCE, that brought farming and husbandry to pottery-using hunter-gatherers north of the Elbe and Vistula rivers.

michelsberg-culture.name: Michelsberg culture
michelsberg-culture.summary: A Neolithic culture of Central Europe, dated about 4400 to 3500 BC, spread along both sides of the Rhine and began the European tradition of timber framing.

shoe-last-celt.name: Shoe-last celt
shoe-last-celt.summary: A long, thin polished stone tool for felling trees and woodworking, characteristic of the early Neolithic Linearbandkeramik and Hinkelstein cultures.

lengyel-culture.name: Lengyel culture
lengyel-culture.summary: A European Neolithic archaeological culture centered on the Middle Danube, flourishing from 5000 to 4000 BC before giving way to the Funnelbeaker and Baden cultures.

stroke-ornamented-ware-culture.name: Stroke-ornamented ware culture
stroke-ornamented-ware-culture.summary: A Central European Neolithic culture of about 4900 to 4400 BC that succeeded the Linear Pottery culture, centered on Silesia and spreading eastward.

nitriansky-hr-dok.name: Nitriansky Hrádok
nitriansky-hr-dok.summary: A district of the town of Šurany in Slovakia, annexed to it in 1976.

nebra-sky-disc.name: Nebra sky disc
nebra-sky-disc.summary: A Bronze Age bronze disc inlaid with gold symbols of the sun, moon, and stars, found near Nebra, Germany in 1999 and dated to about 1800 to 1600 BC; the oldest known depiction of astronomical phenomena.

goseck-circle.name: Goseck Circle
goseck-circle.summary: A Neolithic circular enclosure in Germany built around 4900 BC, with entrances aligned to sunrise and sunset on the solstices.

talheim-death-pit.name: Talheim Death Pit
talheim-death-pit.summary: A mass grave discovered in Germany in 1983 in a Linear Pottery Culture settlement, dating to about 5000 BC and containing 34 bodies showing the earliest signs of organized violence in Neolithic Europe.

bronocice.name: Bronocice
bronocice.summary: Village in south-central Poland where a pot was found in 1976 bearing the earliest known image of a wheeled vehicle, dated to about 3635 to 3370 BC.

lower-saxony.name: Lower Saxony
lower-saxony.summary: Coastal state in northwestern Germany, the country's second-largest by land area, spanning both maritime and mountainous terrain.

arsenical-bronze.name: Arsenical bronze
arsenical-bronze.summary: An alloy of copper with arsenic, sometimes combined with tin, valued for making a stronger bronze with better casting behavior.

flintbek.name: Flintbek
flintbek.summary: A municipality in Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, where cart tracks from about 3400 BCE were found under a megalithic long barrow, the earliest known direct evidence of wheeled vehicles anywhere.

hofheim-hesse.name: Hofheim
hofheim-hesse.summary: The administrative centre of the Main-Taunus-Kreis district in Hesse, Germany, near Frankfurt, first documented in 1254.

brittany.name: Brittany
brittany.summary: Peninsula and historical region in northwestern France, homeland of the Breton people, home to some of the world's oldest standing architecture, dating to the early 5th millennium BC.

r-ssen-culture.name: Rössen culture
r-ssen-culture.summary: A middle Neolithic culture of Central Europe, about 4600 to 4300 BCE, named after a burial site in Saxony-Anhalt and marking a shift toward more diverse later Neolithic cultures.

saxony-anhalt.name: Saxony-Anhalt
saxony-anhalt.summary: A German state formed in 1945 from the former Prussian Province of Saxony and the Free State of Anhalt, dissolved in 1952 and re-established after reunification in 1990.

toru.name: Toruń
toru.summary: City on the Vistula River in north-central Poland, one of the country's oldest cities, first settled in the 8th century and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
